title: Who Owns the Past?
objective: After this level you can explain debates over returning ancient objects to Egypt.
summary: Zahi Hawass wants the Rosetta Stone and Nefertiti bust returned; the museums in London and Berlin defend how they got them. Egypt opened the Grand Egyptian Museum in 2025.

cards.headline: The Rosetta Stone has sat in London since 1802. Many want it back.
cards.body: Who should keep objects taken from Egypt long ago? It’s a real argument, and both sides have reasons. Here are both cases, who makes them, and one very large new building.

cards.headline: The case for return
cards.body: In 2022, Zahi Hawass, Egypt’s former antiquities minister, launched a petition for the Rosetta Stone’s return that passed 100,000 signatures. He also wants the bust of Nefertiti back from Berlin and the Dendera Zodiac from the Louvre, saying these unique objects belong in Egypt. On Nefertiti he goes further: he argues the bust, found in 1912 and taken to Berlin in 1913, left Egypt illegally.

cards.headline: The museums’ case
cards.body: The British Museum says the Rosetta Stone came to Britain under an 1801 treaty signed by a representative of Egypt. It adds that Egypt’s government has made no formal request, and that most known copies of the decree are already in Egypt. Berlin’s museum points out that the Nefertiti bust left through an official division of finds in 1913, overseen by an inspector of Egypt’s antiquities service. Same objects, very different stories.

cards.headline: A new home by the pyramids
cards.body: Egypt has also made its point in concrete. The Grand Egyptian Museum, near the Great Pyramid at Giza, officially opened on 1 November 2025 with about 100,000 artifacts. For the first time since its discovery, Tutankhamun’s entire collection is shown together. Remember Carter’s 5,398 numbered objects from Level 95? They’re finally all in one place.

cards.headline: Who owns the past: weighed
learned: Hawass: the Rosetta Stone and Nefertiti belong in Egypt
British Museum: an 1801 treaty and no formal request
Berlin: an official division of finds in 1913
Grand Egyptian Museum opened at Giza in 2025

questions.prompt: In November 2025, Egypt’s Grand Egyptian Museum opened _____.

options.label: near the Great Pyramid at Giza
on the island of Philae
options.rationale: It’s at Giza, by the pyramids.

options.label: by the great temples at Karnak
options.rationale: It’s at Giza, near the Great Pyramid.

questions.explanation: The Grand Egyptian Museum stands near the Great Pyramid at Giza and opened on 1 November 2025.

questions.prompt: Match each object or museum with its description.
questions.explanation: The British Museum points to an 1801 treaty for the Rosetta Stone. Berlin says the Nefertiti bust left through an official division of finds. The Dendera Zodiac is in the Louvre. The Grand Egyptian Museum opened with about 100,000 artifacts.

questions.prompt: Berlin says the Nefertiti bust left Egypt legally in 1913. Where had it been found?

options.label: In Nefertiti’s tomb in the Valley of the Kings
options.rationale: It came from a workshop, not a tomb.

questions.explanation: The bust was found at Amarna in 1912, in the workshop of the sculptor Thutmose.
